item.title: Congress taking first votes on Iran war as debate rages about US goals
item.description: The U.S. Senate is headed towards a vote on President Donald Trump’s decision to embark on a war against Iran. It's an extraordinary test in Congress for a conflict that has rapidly spread across the Middle East with no clear U.S. exit strategy. The legislation is known as a war powers resolution. It gives lawmakers an opportunity to demand congressional approval before any further attacks are carried out. The votes marked a weighty moment for lawmakers. item.title: The Latest: Explosions heard in Tehran and Jerusalem on fifth day of war
item.description: Explosions are sounding in Iran’s capital city as its war with the U.S. and Israel enters a fifth day. Iranian state television reported explosions in Tehran at dawn Wednesday. In Israel, air defenses were activated due to incoming missile fire from Iran and explosions were heard over Jerusalem. item.title: Arizona State beats No. 14 Kansas 70-60 in Hurley’s potential home finale
item.description: Moe Odum scored 23 points, Massamba Diop added 19 and Arizona State pulled away late to beat No. 14 Kansas 70-60 on Tuesday night in what could be Sun Devils coach Bobby Hurley’s final home game. Hurley is the final year of his contract and the administration hasn’t given any indications it will be extended amid a fourth mediocre season in the past five years. item.description: Former Democratic Gov. Roy Cooper and ex-Republican National Committee Chairman Michael Whatley have won their respective party nominations for a North Carolina U.S. Senate seat. Their wins in Tuesday’s primary elections set up a high-stakes showdown in the fall. Both clinched their elections in crowded fields to replace retiring Sen. Thom Tillis. item.title: Atlanta Braves’ Jurickson Profar suspended for 2026 season following second positive drug test
item.description: Atlanta Braves outfielder Jurickson Profar has been suspended for the 2026 season by Major League Baseball following his second positive test for a performance-enhancing drug. Profar tested positive for exogenous testosterone and its metabolites, the commissioner’s office said, which means testosterone that was not produced by his body. item.title: Colts place transition tag on Daniel Jones and Breece Hall gets franchise tag from Jets
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts placed a transition tag on quarterback Daniel Jones and the New York Jets used the franchise tag on running back Breece Hall as teams beat the deadline to place tags on potential free agents. The Colts opted to use the $37.8 million transition tag instead of the $43.9 million franchise tag, opening up the possibility that he could still leave without compensation for Indianapolis.
